comparison: Both evaluate the computational pipeline (C24-C30) as SUPPORTED. Strong agreement on pipeline effectiveness.

Both support statistical filtering approach (C32-C36). OpenEval details Fisher-Yates methodology with 10,000 permutations, peer reviewers confirm 'statistical measure was used to remove potential false positives.' Overlapping claims show methodological agreement.

Both address statistical filtering (C31, C37) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on threshold justification and validation, peer reviewers affirm the statistical approach addresses 'challenges faced by existing approaches.' Complete agreement.

Both support AlphaFold integration (C41-C48). OpenEval emphasizes novel application to predict functional ITIMs with data-driven thresholds, peer reviewers validate this as addressing previous limitations with 'solid justification.' Strong concordance.

Both evaluate AlphaFold filtering (C38-C40, C43-C44) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details hypothesis about ITIMs in disordered regions, peer reviewers confirm AlphaFold 'filter[s] out putative receptors that are low confidence.' Agreement on methodological strength.

Both support structural characterization (C49-C50). OpenEval validates percentages and methodological importance of isoform distinction, peer reviewers accept this as part of comprehensive expression analysis. Agreement on descriptive claims.

Both evaluate expression analysis (C51-C64) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes internally consistent quantitative results with biologically plausible patterns, peer reviewers call it 'reasonable and appropriate first step' for understanding differential expression. Strong agreement.

Both support multi-spanning receptor expression analysis (C65-C72). OpenEval notes consistent methodology and interesting biological findings, peer reviewers acknowledge identification of 'single- and multi-spanning targets' without challenge. Complete agreement.

Divergence in evaluation: OpenEval rates functional categorization (C73-C107) as UNCERTAIN due to arbitrary thresholds and limited in vitro validation, while peer reviewers rate it SUPPORTED as 'reasonable and appropriate first step.' Peer reviewers more accepting of computational predictions.

Both address multi-spanning functional categorization (C108-C112). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with consistent methodology, peer reviewers also SUPPORTED as part of functional lens approach. Agreement despite OpenEval's concerns about single-spanning categorization.

Both evaluate tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte analysis (C118-C130) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes biological plausibility of differentiated T cell findings, peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge as 'proof-of-concept' analysis. Strong agreement with appropriate caveats.

Both support validation against known targets (C131-C133). OpenEval notes this strengthens confidence despite in vitro limitations, peer reviewers confirm pipeline 'can be used to rediscover known targets.' Complete agreement on validation approach.

Both evaluate methodological improvements (C137-C142) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details specific advantages of TOPCONS and novel filtering, peer reviewers explicitly recognize 'solid justification' for addressing previous challenges. Strong concordance with high Jaccard index (0.714).

Both support AlphaFold limitations discussion (C144-C148). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of threshold exclusions, peer reviewers implicitly accept by validating overall pipeline. Agreement on transparent limitation acknowledgment.

Both address AlphaFold threshold limitations (C145-C148). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with transparent acknowledgment of CD5/BTLA exclusion, peer reviewers affirm AlphaFold approach addresses challenges. Agreement on methodological trade-offs.

Both support limitation acknowledgments (C149-C150). OpenEval emphasizes 98% recall with honest assessment of potential biases, peer reviewers recognize statistical and structural filtering strengths. Agreement on balanced presentation.

Both evaluate limitations (C151-C157) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides thorough assessment of subcellular localization and scope limitations, peer reviewers acknowledge 'lack of direct experimental validation' as reasonable for computational study. Strong agreement on appropriate caveats.

Both address multi-spanning receptors (C158-C161). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative immune inhibition claims, peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED by accepting identification without challenging functional speculation. Mild divergence in interpretation stringency.

OpenEval rates combination therapy speculation (C165) as UNCERTAIN without experimental support, peer reviewers SUPPORTED functional categorization framework as established from prior work. Divergence reflects different evaluation of hypothesis-generating vs. validated findings.

Divergence: OpenEval rates biological interpretations (C166-C169) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative functional claims, peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED as 'reasonable and appropriate first step.' Peer reviewers more accepting of expression-based inferences.

Both evaluate isoform and ligand limitations (C170-C174) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these as significant caveats for functional interpretation, peer reviewers accept as reasonable limitations. Complete agreement on appropriate acknowledgment.

Both support main findings summary (C135, C191-C194). OpenEval validates 98% recall and comprehensive integration, peer reviewers confirm 'solid evidence' for pipeline effectiveness. Strong agreement on overall contribution.

Both address drug target selection support (C194). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as reasonable given comprehensive data, peer reviewers affirm pipeline 'will support future drug target selection.' Complete agreement on practical utility.

Peer reviewers explicitly supported background/rationale claims (C1-C7, C16-C23, C197-C199) without challenge, treating them as established context. OpenEval did not separately evaluate these foundational claims, focusing instead on novel contributions.

Peer reviewers supported future directions and applications (C175-C180, C183, C186-C187, C189) as reasonable extensions. OpenEval did not separately evaluate these forward-looking claims, which represent proposed rather than demonstrated findings.
